question: Create a concept interior model of the real Suzhou Museum New Building by I.M. Pei, focusing on a white geometric exhibition gallery opening through a framed doorway and hexagonal window toward a semi-open water courtyard.

target.architect: I.M. Pei with Pei Partnership Architects
target.scope: Main gallery / central hall / cloister / water courtyard interface

channels.agent_reach: unavailable in this environment; Codex web research used as the research channel
channels.official_museum: passed via official museum story and museum pages
channels.academic_reference: found but not used as a measurement source

sources.title: Suzhou Museum official introduction: Pei and Suzhou Museum
evidence: The museum describes inner courtyards as a device that connects interior and exterior space.
The new building has a main courtyard and several smaller inner courtyards.

sources.title: Suzhou Museum: I.M. Pei Masterwork - Google Arts & Culture
evidence: The museum was completed in 2006 and designed by I.M. Pei.
The entrance hall connects to other museum functions.
The hall uses a geometric roof frame with square and triangular lines.
High angled windows bring sky views into the interior.
White walls, dark roof tones, glass and steel create the visual language.
The museum includes a two-story steel stair and a water-lotus courtyard.

sources.title: AD Classics: Suzhou Museum / I.M. Pei + Pei Partnership Architects
evidence: The plan wraps a central water court with a rectangular building composition.
Exhibition halls are organized around cloisters and form an enclosed network around the internal courtyard.
The central hall rises through an octagonal and folded geometric roof form with natural light.
The design uses whitewashed plaster walls, dark gray roof material and garden architecture.

sources.title: Suzhou Museum spatial syntax research - Palace Museum academic source
evidence: The public space is described as a courtyard-based layout where modern and historic architecture coexist.
The spatial experience is organized through movement, gardens and changing views.

research_limits: The selected interior zone is a concept synthesis, not an exact survey of one room.
Exact wall thicknesses, door schedule and room dimensions are inferred from public plans and photos.
The model intentionally combines a closed gallery with a semi-open courtyard edge to test the workflow rule.
